name: Chana Madra
subtitle: chickpeas simmered slowly in whisked yogurt until the gravy is silky, faintly sour and heavy with whole spice

ingredients.note: sour, day-old curd is better than fresh
madra is a generous dish; do not cut this below 4 tbsp
stabilises the yogurt so it will not split
use compounded-free hing to keep this gluten-free
sonth carries the warmth that ginger root would in a plains curry
the Chamba touch, a sweet note against the sour curd

prepNotes: Soak the chickpeas overnight in plenty of water. They should more than double.
Take the yogurt out of the fridge an hour ahead. Cold yogurt splits the moment it meets hot ghee.
Whisk the yogurt with the besan and a pinch of salt until there is not a single lump, then keep the whisk in the bowl - you will use it again.

steps.text: Pressure cook the drained chickpeas with 500ml water and 1 tsp salt for 4 whistles, then let the pressure drop by itself. They should crush easily between finger and thumb but still hold their shape.
steps.tip: Undercooked chana will never soften later - the acid in the yogurt sets them hard.

steps.text: Heat the ghee in a heavy kadhai until it thins and shimmers. Add the cumin, cinnamon, black cardamom, green cardamom, cloves and bay leaves and let them swell and crackle, about 40 seconds.
Add the asafoetida, count to five, then take the pan off the heat entirely and let it cool for a full minute.
steps.tip: This off-heat pause is the whole trick of madra. Yogurt going into ripping-hot ghee will curdle every time.

steps.text: Pour in the whisked yogurt, return to the lowest possible flame and stir continuously in one direction for 8 to 10 minutes, until the yogurt loses its raw smell and thickens to the consistency of pouring cream.
steps.tip: Do not stop stirring and do not cover the pan until the yogurt has come to a boil once.

steps.text: Stir in the coriander powder, fennel powder, dry ginger, turmeric and kashmiri chilli. Cook 3 minutes more - the gravy will turn glossy and the ghee will start to bead at the edges.
Add the drained chickpeas along with 150ml of their cooking water. Season with salt.
Simmer uncovered on low for 20 to 25 minutes, stirring every few minutes, until the gravy coats the back of a spoon and a clear rim of ghee sits around the edge of the pan.
steps.tip: That ring of separated ghee is how Chamba cooks judge madra is done.

steps.text: Fold in the almonds and raisins and cook 3 minutes so the raisins plump.
Finish with the garam masala, cover and rest off the heat for 10 minutes before serving with plain rice.

storage: Keeps 3 days refrigerated and genuinely improves on day two. Reheat very gently on low with a splash of water - a hard boil will break the yogurt.
